To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have synthesized novel prodrugs of highly lipophilic azoles which are water soluble, stable in plasma, and rapidly converted to parent compounds in human plasma.
the novel water-soluble benzylazolyl prodrugs of azole antifungal drugs were synthesized and evaluated.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the synthesis and evaluation of water-soluble prodrugs of highly lipophilic antifungal agents.
the synthesis of novel water soluble prodrugs of azoles.
the development of a novel water-soluble prodrug of highly lipophilic azoles.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the benzylazolyl N-benzylimide or N-benzyl triazole prodrugs are stable, water-soluble prodrugs of highly lipophilic antifungal azoles, which undergo an enzymatic hydrolysis followed by a self-debenzylation to release the parent drug.
the benzylazolyl prodrugs are stable and soluble in water, but are rapidly converted to parent drugs in plasma.
the benzylazol-ium prodrugs were successfully synthesized, characterized, and evaluated for their potential as prodrugs of azole antifungal agents.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the N-alkylazolium type prodrug approach is a promising strategy for the design of novel prodrugs of highly lipophilic azoles.
we have successfully developed a new prodrug strategy for the development of water-soluble, parenterally applicable, prodrugs of highly lipophilic azoles.
the prodrugs of highly lipophilic drugs can be designed to be water soluble prodrugs and to be rapidly and quantitatiavely converted to the parent drugs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the benzylazolyl moiety of the benzylazole antifungal prodrug is a promising candidate for the development of new prodrugs of antifungals.
the benzylazolyl prodrug concept can be applied successfully to several lipophilic azoles and that the resulting prodrugs are promising for parenteral administration.
the benzyltriazolyl prodrugs of azole antifungal drugs can be used for parenteral application and the benzylimidazolyl prodrug of fluconazole can be considered for parenteral use.
